title: 1993 AHSME Problem 10
statement: Let \(r\) be the number that results when both the base and the exponent of \(a^b\) are tripled, where \(a,\) \(b\gt0.\) If \(r\) equals the product of \(a^b\) and \(x^b\) where \(x\gt0,\) then \(x=\)

solutions.text: We have \[ r=(3a)^{3b}=\bigl(27a^3\bigr)^b. \] Also \(r=a^bx^b=(ax)^b.\) Positivity allows us to equate the bases, so \(ax=27a^3\) and \(x=27a^2.\) Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Rewrite the equality so both sides are \(b\)th powers
